title: Green beans, fresh, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Green beans are young pods of the common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) harvested before the seeds fully mature. When cooked with butter or margarine, they retain a crisp texture and acquire a delicate, buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans are a good source of B‑vitamins, vitamin C, and potassium.
Cooking them with fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients.
They are known as "green beans" in the US and "haricots verts" in France.
The French‑style bean is a thinner variety prized for its tenderness.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 35 kcal, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vitamin C, vitamin K, and folate contribute to immune function, blood clotting, and cell health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and plant compounds can lower cholesterol.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beans.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked beans may contain phytohemagglutinin, which can cause gastrointestinal upset.

items.title: Sodium content in added fats
items.content: When using salted butter or margarine, monitor sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steam or sauté the beans in a small amount of butter or margarine until tender but still crisp. Season with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon. Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or tossed into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh beans in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or container for 3‑5 days. Cooked beans can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
